bug_description.original: Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5725002489004032 Project: sleuthkit Fuzzing Engine: afl Fuzz Target: sleuthkit_fls_hfs_fuzzer Job Type: afl_asan_sleuthkit Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 Crash Address: 0x60d000000a8b Crash State: hfs_dir_open_meta_cb hfs_cat_traverse hfs_dir_open_meta Sanitizer: address (ASAN) Reproducer Testcase: https://oss-fuzz.com/download?testcase_id=5725002489004032
bug_description.normalized: The staged HFS image drives Sleuth Kit's catalog traversal over a catalog leaf node whose decoded `nodesize` is 137 and whose offset-table entry `rec_off` points to a key that still fits inside that node. `hfs_cat_traverse` passes `cur_key = &node[rec_off]` into `hfs_dir_open_meta_cb`; the caller's `keylen <= nodesize - rec_off` check proves only that the key bytes fit in the node. The callback then aliases `rec_buf = (uint8_t *)cur_key`, derives `rec_off2` from the same key length, and applies `if ((nodesize < 2) || (rec_off2 >= nodesize - 2))` to that rebased pointer without accounting for `rec_off`, so it does not establish that the payload or a full `hfs_folder` remains after the key. The saved crash at `tsk/fs/hfs_dent.c:274` shows the later `rec_type` read still succeeds on this witness and selects `HFS_FOLDER_RECORD`, after which the folder branch casts `&rec_buf[rec_off2]` to `hfs_folder *` with no `sizeof(hfs_folder)` extent check. Because `folder->std.cnid` starts 8 bytes into that structure, the later `tsk_getu32(folder->std.cnid)` read touches `node[rec_off + rec_off2 + 8 .. rec_off + rec_off2 + 11]`, which is not fully inside the 137-byte heap node buffer allocated in `hfs_cat_traverse`, and AddressSanitizer reports the resulting heap-buffer-overflow at `tsk/fs/hfs_dent.c:274`.

source.description: First project-side decode on the crashing path that materializes the attacker-controlled catalog B-tree node size used for the heap allocation and every later bounds comparison.
source.value_from: The staged HFS image controls `hfs->catalog_header.nodesize`. In the saved ASan run, the immediately following allocation at line 758 creates a 137-byte region, so this decode yields `nodesize = 137` for the crashing node.
source.note: This local `nodesize` is the vulnerability-relevant size state for the rest of the trace.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The callback reads the 4-byte `cnid` field from a truncated folder record whose payload extends past the end of the 137-byte node buffer.
sink.note: Through the `folder` alias, this statement reads the four `std.cnid` bytes at node offsets `rec_off + rec_off2 + 8 .. +11`. AddressSanitizer reports that access here as `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1`, on an address 2 bytes to the right of the 137-byte region allocated in `hfs_cat_traverse`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `hfs_cat_traverse` proves only that the key bytes at `node[rec_off .. rec_off + rec_off2 - 1]` fit inside the node. After the callback rebases `rec_buf = node + rec_off`, the folder branch aliases `rec_buf + rec_off2` as a full `hfs_folder` without a `sizeof(hfs_folder)` check, while the preceding `rec_off2 >= nodesize - 2` test compares that rebased offset only against the full node size and therefore does not prove the remaining bytes after `rec_off` can hold the structure.
root_cause.note: The staged vulnerable source itself shows the missing obligation: the adjacent `HFS_FILE_RECORD` branch performs a `sizeof(hfs_file)` extent check before casting, but `HFS_FOLDER_RECORD` reaches this cast immediately.

parser_admitted.code:
a_cb(hfs, HFS_BT_NODE_TYPE_LEAF, key, keylen, nodesize,
                    cur_off + rec_off, ptr);
parser_admitted.description: Once the current catalog leaf record's offset-table entry and key length pass the caller's node-local checks, `hfs_cat_traverse` dispatches `key = &node[rec_off]` to `hfs_dir_open_meta_cb` as `cur_key`, together with the decoded `keylen` and `nodesize`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This read materializes the attacker-controlled catalog node bytes into the exact `nodesize`-byte heap buffer later overread.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: On the crashing run, `nodesize` is 137, so `tsk_fs_attr_read` fills a 137-byte heap node buffer whose contents later supply `key->key_len`, `rec_type`, and the truncated folder payload.

coarse_trace.summary: Catalog traversal decodes attacker-controlled `nodesize = 137`, allocates a 137-byte heap buffer for the current catalog node, and reads that node's bytes from the HFS image.

The leaf walker decodes the attack-controlled record offset `rec_off` from the node's offset table, validates only that the key at `node[rec_off]` fits inside the node, and dispatches that same pointer to `hfs_dir_open_meta_cb`.

Inside the callback, `rec_buf = (uint8_t *)cur_key` preserves the `node + rec_off` base, `rec_off2` is recomputed from the key length, and the callback only compares that rebased offset against the full `nodesize`, so it does not prove that the payload after the key still fits inside the remaining bytes of the node.

The saved crash at line 274 shows the later `rec_type` read reaches the `HFS_FOLDER_RECORD` arm; that branch aliases `&node[rec_off + rec_off2]` as `hfs_folder *` without a `sizeof(hfs_folder)` check, and the later `folder->std.cnid` read at offsets `rec_off + rec_off2 + 8 .. +11` crosses the 137-byte heap buffer.

fine_trace.note: The HFS catalog header controls the local node size used on this traversal. The saved ASan allocation stack proves the witness makes this decode produce `nodesize = 137`.
Allocates the heap buffer that will hold the current catalog node. ASan identifies this allocation as a 137-byte region, which is the destination extent later overread.
Reads the attacker-controlled catalog node bytes into the 137-byte heap buffer. The later key length, record type, and truncated folder payload are all interpreted from this buffer.
The leaf-node offset table is attacker-controlled. For the crashing record it yields the node-relative start `rec_off`, and every later callback address is relative to `node + rec_off`.

The leaf walker treats `node + rec_off` as `key`, computes `keylen`, rejects only keys that exceed `nodesize - rec_off`, and then passes that same pointer to `hfs_dir_open_meta_cb` as `cur_key` with `cur_keylen = keylen`. That admission proves the key bytes fit in the node, not that the payload after the key does.

Inside the callback, `rec_buf` aliases the same address as `cur_key`, so on this path `rec_buf == node + rec_off`. Subsequent `rec_off2` and `folder` calculations therefore become absolute node offsets when added to `rec_off`.

The callback recomputes the payload offset relative to `rec_buf` and then checks that rebased offset only against the full `nodesize`. Because `rec_buf == node + rec_off`, this test does not establish that bytes remain after `rec_off`; the earlier caller check proved only that the key itself ends no later than `node[nodesize]`, not that the post-key payload or a full `hfs_folder` fits.

The saved crash at line 274 inside the `HFS_FOLDER_RECORD` branch shows this read completes on the witness and that `rec_type` selects that arm. That control-flow fact comes from reaching the later sink, not from step 7's rebased `nodesize` check; the code still has not established that a full folder record fits after `rec_off`.

The folder branch now aliases `node[rec_off + rec_off2]` as a full `hfs_folder` even though the staged vulnerable source has no `sizeof(hfs_folder)` check here. In `tsk_hfs.h`, `folder->std.cnid` starts 8 bytes into `hfs_folder`, so this alias makes the later read target node offsets `rec_off + rec_off2 + 8 .. +11`, which are not fully inside the 137-byte allocation on the witness path.

The callback reads the four-byte `cnid` field through that truncated `folder` alias. On the saved run, ASan reports the resulting heap-buffer-overflow at this line against the 137-byte node allocation from `hfs_cat_traverse`.

allocation_context.note: ASan's allocation stack identifies the `tsk_malloc(nodesize)` call that created the overread 137-byte node buffer.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` does not match the vulnerable source under `_work/src/sleuthkit`: it changes `rec_off2 >= nodesize - sizeof(hfs_folder)` to `rec_off2 > ...` in a folder-branch check that is absent from the staged vulnerable `tsk/fs/hfs_dent.c`. Stage 02 therefore does not use that patch metadata as proof that this traced path is fixed.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, patch.diff, and the vulnerable Sleuth Kit checkout under `_work/src/sleuthkit`

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context fixes the destination extent at the 137-byte node buffer; the root cause is the later missing folder-record size check before reading from that allocation.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run on the exact staged `poc` reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `hfs_dir_open_meta_cb`, with stack `hfs_dir_open_meta_cb -> hfs_cat_traverse -> hfs_dir_open_meta`, while `sleuthkit_fls_hfs_fuzzer` processed the HFS image.

format.name: HFS+ filesystem image
format.contract: The staged image must make `hfs_cat_traverse` read a 137-byte catalog leaf node whose offset-table entry `rec_off` points at a key that passes the caller's `keylen <= nodesize - rec_off` check, then make `hfs_dir_open_meta_cb` rebase `rec_buf = node + rec_off`, derive `rec_off2` from that key, survive the callback's full-node `rec_off2 >= nodesize - 2` guard, and reach the `HFS_FOLDER_RECORD` branch while the 4-byte `folder->std.cnid` field at `node[rec_off + rec_off2 + 8 .. rec_off + rec_off2 + 11]` is not fully inside `node[0..136]`.
